claims.text: Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations provide a persistent source of dislocation resistance in concentrated alloys.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations dominate strengthening relative to elastic-misfit contributions.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations govern the broader deformation behavior of multi-component concentrated alloys.
Controlled thermal processing promotes specific chemical short-range ordering in these alloys.
As-cast or quenched FCC MEAs/HEAs are random solid solutions.
As-cast or quenched FCC MEAs/HEAs possess inherent chemical inhomogeneity.
Annealing can modify local chemical short-range order and thereby modify local shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
Thermal activation at ambient to moderately elevated temperatures can promote ordering without full homogenization.
Enhanced short-range ordering creates localized hard atomic motifs with elevated shear-fault energy.
Thermal treatment increases the amplitude of local shear-fault-energy fluctuations by promoting chemical short-range order.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations act as strong pinning points that impede dislocation motion.
Pinning by local shear-fault-energy fluctuations can reduce twinning or favor alternative slip mechanisms.
Greater local shear-fault-energy fluctuations will produce higher yield strength.
Thermally processed alloys will exhibit more pronounced dislocation pinning than as-cast alloys.
Thermally processed alloys may exhibit diminished twinning relative to as-cast alloys.
As-cast alloys have lower shear-fault-energy fluctuations than the proposed thermally processed alloys.
As-cast alloys undergo conventional dislocation motion and consequently have relatively lower yield strength.
The proposed mechanism should hold for FCC MEAs/HEAs under moderate temperature and strain-rate regimes.
Other mechanisms may dominate in alternate crystal structures or under extreme loading or temperature conditions.
Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in yield strength or altered dislocation pinning in the processed group would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that shear-fault-energy fluctuations dominate strength, while the uncertainty field says their quantitative importance relative to grain-size and elastic-misfit strengthening is not fully established.
